skill.name: effect-queues-background
skill.description: Queue and PubSub patterns, background fibers, and graceful shutdown. Use for decoupling producers/consumers.
skill.body:
# Queues, PubSub & Background

## When to use
- Decoupling producers/consumers with backpressure
- Broadcasting events to multiple subscribers
- Running background loops with graceful shutdown

## Queue (bounded)
```ts
import { Queue } from "effect"
const q = yield* Queue.bounded<string>(32)
yield* Queue.offer(q, "job")
const job = yield* Queue.take(q)
```

## PubSub (broadcast)
```ts
import { PubSub } from "effect"
const ps = yield* PubSub.bounded<string>(32)
yield* PubSub.publish(ps, "evt")
```

## Background Fiber
```ts
const fiber = yield* Effect.fork(loop)
yield* Fiber.interrupt(fiber)
```

## Guidance
- Prefer bounded queues to apply natural backpressure
- Use multiple workers by forking consumers
- Ensure background fibers are interrupted during shutdown

## Pitfalls
- Unbounded queues lead to memory growth
- Silent background failures → add logging/metrics

## Cross-links
- Concurrency for pools and interruption
- Time/Logging for observability of background tasks

generated_query: I'm building a notification service that processes incoming events from a message queue. I need to spawn a background fiber that continuously polls for new events, processes them, and sends notifications. I also want to broadcast certain high-priority events to multiple notification channels (email, SMS). I need to handle graceful shutdown so that when the application stops, the background fiber finishes its current job and then exits cleanly. Can you show me how to implement this using Effect’s Queue and PubSub?

- Interrupting a fiber mid‑process may leave work unfinished
- PubSub subscribers must be created before publishing
